question: The Consular Digitalisation Plan of the Spanish Ministry of Foreign Affairs, European Union and Cooperation has been granted EUR 115 million in NextGenerationEU funds under component 11 of Spain’s Recovery, Transformation and Resilience Plan (RTRP). The ministry has linked the digitalisation in question to its capacity to process applications for citizenship under what is known as the grandchildren’s law1.

In addition, the Border Management and Visa Instrument (BMVI) provides EUR 30 million in EU funding to support consular offices and Schengen visa points. At the same time, the Spanish consulate in Havana has concluded a contract worth EUR 1 131 295.

68 (plus VAT) with Palco, a Cuban state-owned company, subcontracting it to provide between 88 and 107 workers who, according to press reports, could access sensitive personal data relating to those applying for Spanish nationality under the grandchildren’s law. In view of the above: 1.
Can the Commission confirm whether the reinforcement of the consulate staff by Cuban company Palco is funded, directly or indirectly, under component 11 of the RTRP or under the BMVI?
Has Spain established before the Commission that the NextGenerationEU funds linked to consular digitalisation do not pay for functions carried out by the staff of a non-EU state entity?
If EU funds have been earmarked for this contract, what action does the Commission intend to take?
Eighth additional provision of Spanish Law 20/2022 of 19 October 2022 on democratic memory: https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2022-17099. 1
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (7.10.2026) The Spanish authorities have confirmed that no contract, agreement or other legal instrument is associated with PALCO or the PALCO Group in their Recovery and Resilience Facility information system Componente de Fondos Europeos, whether under component 11 or any other component.

While a service contract between the Consulate General of Spain in Havana and Grupo PALCO for an amount of EUR 1 131 295.68 is in place, the procurement documents, which can be found on the Spanish public sector procurement platform, expressly state that the contract is not financed by EU funds1.

The Recovery and Resilience Facility disburses payments based on the Member State’s positive fulfilment of the milestones and targets as set out in the Annex to the Council Implementing Decision (CID)2. The Commission then assesses their implementation exclusively against the specific requirements set out in the Annex to the CID.

The milestones and targets set out in investments 1, 2, 3, and 6 of component 11 of the Spanish Recovery and Resilience Plan concern the digital transformation of the public administration and the reinforcement of its cybersecurity capabilities.

None of the milestones and targets related to these investments, in particular, M162, T164, M166, M167, M169, and M175b, lay down requirements concerning the contractors or staff responsible for the digitalisation.
